title: One-arm Pull-ups - B
texts:
This workout is designed to help you work towards consolidating your one-arm pull-up strength. This workout is designed for climbers who are close to completing or can complete a one-arm pull-up on a good day. This training helps develop maximal pulling strength for climbing.

Part 1 of the workout contains assisted one-arm pull-ups. Use enough assistance which will allow you to complete the workout sets and reps in good form in full. This may mean you use no assistance on rep one but some assistance on reps 2 and 3. During the last reps of the workout, you should be close to failure due to the high intensity. This will mean you are developing maximal strength. If you cannot complete the listed volume, increase the assistance used on your next session or bring in the use of assistance earlier in the set.

You can start the pull-up with a slight bend in your elbow if this is more comfortable. Switch arms between sets to create a rest period of 3-4 minutes between the same arm being used.

You can either use a resistance band or pulley setup to create the correct assistance. Please note how much assistance was used to track progress.

Rest at least 5 minutes before part 2.

Part 2 of the workout involves one-arm negative pull-ups. Using an eccentric (lengthening) movement will help overload the muscles further and help develop more strength. 

We would suggest that to make the most of this workout; you should aim to complete the sets and reps at body weight. Pull up using two arms or stand on a block to begin the movement at the highest part of a one-arm pull-up. From the highest point, slowly lower down using just one arm until you reach a fully straight position. Keep alternating arms within the set. This means you lower on one arm, then the other alternating for a total of 3 reps on each arm per set. There are 3 sets in total.

A timer will help you manage your lowering time. Each rep is 5 seconds allowing for 2 seconds to pull up on two arms and 3 seconds to lower on one arm. There are 6 reps of 5 seconds per set (3 on each arm).
